'''Andrew James Granville''' (born 7 September 1962) is a British mathematician, working in the field of [[number theory]].

== Education ==
Granville received his Bachelor of Arts (Honours) (1983) and his [[Part III of the Mathematical Tripos|Certificate of Advanced Studies (Distinction)]] (1984) from [[Trinity College, Cambridge|Trinity College, Cambridge University]]. He received his PhD from [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]] in 1987<ref name=":0">{{MathGenealogy|id=5613}}</ref> and was inducted into the [[Royal Society of Canada]] in 2006.

== Career ==
He has been a faculty member at the [[Université de Montréal]] since 2002. Before moving to Montreal he was a mathematics professor at the [[University of Georgia]] (UGA) from 1991 until 2002. During his postdoctoral years, he worked at the [[University of Toronto]] and the [[Institute for Advanced Study]]. He was a section speaker in the 1994 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] together with [[Carl Pomerance]] from UGA.<ref name=":0" />

=== Research ===
{{Expand section|date=May 2024|small=no}}
Granville's work is mainly in [[number theory]], in particular [[analytic number theory]]. Along with [[Carl Pomerance]] and [[W. R. (Red) Alford]] he proved the infinitude of [[Carmichael numbers]] in 1994.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=W. R. Alford |author2=Andrew Granville |author3=Carl Pomerance |title=There are infinitely many Carmichael numbers |journal=Annals of Mathematics |volume=139 |year=1994 |pages=703–722 |doi=10.2307/2118576 |mr=1283874 |url=http://math.dartmouth.edu/~carlp/PDF/paper95.pdf |issue=3 |jstor=2118576 }}</ref> This proof was based on a conjecture given by [[Paul Erdős]].

=== Awards ===
Granville was the first recipient of the [[Ribenboim Prize]] of the Canadian Number Theory Association, in 1999. Granville won a [[Lester R. Ford Award]] in 2007<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Andrew Granville |author2=Greg Martin |title=Prime Number Races|journal=Amer. Math. Monthly|volume=113|issue=1 |year=2006|pages=1–33|url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/prime-number-races|doi=10.2307/27641834|jstor=27641834 }}</ref> and again in 2009.<ref>{{cite journal|author =Andrew Granville|title=Prime Number Patterns|journal=Amer. Math. Monthly|volume=115|issue=4|year=2008|pages=279–296|jstor=27642472|url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/prime-number-patterns|doi=10.1080/00029890.2008.11920529|s2cid=2924252}}</ref> In 2008, he won the [[Chauvenet Prize]] for expository writing from the [[Mathematical Association of America]] for his paper ''"It is easy to determine whether a given integer is prime"''.<ref>{{cite journal |author =Andrew Granville |title=It is easy to determine whether a given integer is prime |journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |volume=42 |issue=1 |year=2005 |pages=3–38 |doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-04-01037-7 |mr=2115065 |url=https://www.ams.org/bull/2005-42-01/S0273-0979-04-01037-7/S0273-0979-04-01037-7.pdf|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.maa.org/Awards/chauvent.html |title=MAA Chauvenet Prize page |access-date=18 January 2008 |archive-date=6 April 2003 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030406211448/http://www.maa.org/Awards/chauvent.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 19 January 2013.</ref>

=== Other ===
Andrew Granville, in collaboration with his sister Jennifer Granville, a film writer,<ref name="maa">[https://maa.org/news/interview-andrew-granville An Interview with Andrew Granville], 2008</ref> wrote ''[[Prime Suspects: The Anatomy of Integers and Permutations]]'', a graphic novel that is a "mathematical detective story"<ref name="maa" /> and investigates key concepts in mathematics.<ref>{{cite book | author1=Andrew Granville |author2=Jennifer Granville |title=Prime Suspects: The Anatomy of Integers and Permutations  | publisher=Princeton University Press|year=2019|isbn=978-0-691-14915-8}}</ref>
